name: 46,XY Difference of Sex Development Due to Adrenal and Testicular Steroidogenesis Defect

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and biochemical diagnostic criteria for 46,XY DSD due to steroidogenesis defect

criteria.description: Presence of ambiguous or undervirilized external genitalia in a 46,XY individual
Biochemical evidence of impaired adrenal and testicular steroidogenesis (e.g., low testosterone, elevated precursors)
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes involved in adrenal and testicular steroidogenesis
Imaging or surgical evidence of absent or rudimentary Müllerian structures
Positive family history of DSD or related steroidogenesis defects

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of ambiguous genitalia in a 46,XY individual plus biochemical evidence of steroidogenesis defect and genetic confirmation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires multidisciplinary evaluation including endocrinology, genetics, and radiology.

searchTerms: ambiguous male genitalia with underdeveloped male features

pathognomonic.symptomName: Impaired testosterone synthesis evidenced by low serum testosterone

searchTerms: high levels of adrenal hormone precursors
late or missing male puberty changes
urethral opening on underside of penis

occasional.symptomName: Salt-wasting crisis due to adrenal insufficiency
occasional.notes: More common in severe adrenal steroidogenesis defects

searchTerms: breast tissue growth in teenage boys

occasional.symptomName: Müllerian remnants detected on imaging or surgery
searchTerms: presence of female reproductive tissue remnants
mild low sodium or high potassium levels

rare.symptomName: Adrenal crisis with hypotension and shock
searchTerms: adrenal crisis causing low blood pressure and shock

rare.symptomName: Psychiatric manifestations related to gender identity issues
searchTerms: mental health issues related to gender identity
male infertility from sperm production problems

laboratory: Low serum testosterone and dihydrotestosterone levels
imaging: Ultrasound or MRI showing absent or rudimentary Müllerian structures
Undescended testes visualized in inguinal canal or abdomen
genetic: Pathogenic variants in genes such as CYP17A1, HSD3B2, STAR, or POR
other: Histopathology of gonadal tissue showing dysgenetic testes or Leydig cell hypoplasia

distinguishingFeatures: Normal or elevated testosterone levels with androgen receptor defects
Presence of female external genitalia despite 46,XY karyotype
Normal testosterone but low dihydrotestosterone levels

redFlags: Severe ambiguous genitalia requiring urgent multidisciplinary evaluation
Signs of adrenal crisis such as vomiting, dehydration, hypotension
Failure to thrive or electrolyte disturbances in neonate
references: Hughes IA, et al. Consensus statement on management of intersex disorders. Arch Dis Child. 2006.
